summary: Joseph Tiefenthaler (1710–1785) was a Jesuit missionary from 1729 to 1773 who worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Rector of Agra Jesuit College around 1744–1747.

Joseph Toussaint Reinaud (1795–1867) studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy in 1815. Working in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, he held posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France and the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales.

Joseph Vendryes (1875–1960) was a linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet, Victor Henry, Sylvain Lévi, and Rudolf Thurneysen. He held posts at the University of Paris, École Normale Supérieure, and École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Joseph Virgil Grohmann (1831–1919) was an Indologist and linguist who completed a Ph.D. at Charles University, studying under Georg Curtius and August Schleicher. He later held posts at Prager Handelsakademie, Leitmeritzer Oberrealschule, and Landesschulrat.

Joseph Walker Jasper Ouseley (1800–1889) worked in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at Fort William College, East India Company College (1844–1859), the Civil Service Commission (1862–1883), and King's College London.

Joseph Walser works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Isshi Yamada, Adolf von Wuertenberg, and David S. Pacini, and was affiliated with Loyola University Chicago as attested in 1998.

Joseph Wright (1855–1930) was a linguist who studied at Yorkshire College, the University of Leipzig, and Heidelberg University, earning a Ph.D. under Hermann Osthoff. He later served at the University of Oxford and Corpus Christi College, Oxford.

Joseph van den Gheyn (1854–1913) was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and linguistics who studied under Charles-Joseph de Harlez de Deulin at KU Leuven. He held posts at KU Leuven, Collège Saint-Michel, Institut Catholique de Paris, and the Bibliothèque nationale de France.

Joseph von Hammer-Purgstall (1774–1856) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and history and archaeology. He studied at the K.k. Akademie für Orientalische Sprachen (circa 1789–1799) and later held a post at the Austrian Academy of Sciences.
Josho Nozawa studied under Susumu Yamaguchi. Working in the fields of Buddhist studies and Indology, he held a professorship at Koyasan University, attested in 1950.

Joshu Sasaki (1907–2014) worked in Buddhist studies, studying at Zuiryo-ji and under Joten Soko Miura. He served as abbot at Yotoku-in and Shojuan, and founded the Mount Baldy Zen Center, where he was abbot until 2012.

Joshua Ereshefsky works in Buddhist and religious studies. As attested in 2026, he is a PhD candidate in religious studies at McMaster University, where he studied under doctoral supervisor James A. Benn.

Joshua Marshman (1768–1837) worked in Indology, Sinology, and linguistics. He studied at Bristol Baptist College (~1794–1799) and under Johannes Lassar (~1805–1812), and founded Serampore College in 1818.

Joshua Timothy Katz (born 1969) is a linguist educated at Yale, Oxford, and Harvard. He held a professorship at Princeton University (1998–2022) and later served as a Senior Fellow at the American Enterprise Institute.
Joshua W. C. Cutler works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Geshe Wangyal and held a post at the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center, attested in 2004.
Joshua Whatmough (1897–1964) was a linguist who studied at the University of Manchester and Emmanuel College. He held academic posts at Bangor University, Cairo University, and Harvard University.

Josiah Royce (1855–1916) was a philosopher who studied at the University of California, Berkeley, the University of Göttingen under Hermann Lotze, and Johns Hopkins University. He held academic posts at Berkeley, Johns Hopkins, and Harvard University.

Josip Florschütz (1864–1916) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He earned a Ph.D. from the University of Vienna (1882–1885) and became an associate professor at the University of Zagreb in 1908.

José Alemany y Bolufer (1866–1934) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Pedro Roca y López, at the University of Barcelona, and at Complutense University of Madrid. He later held professorships at the University of Granada and Complutense University.

José Canedo Grille (1902–1945) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Seminario Mayor de Santiago de Compostela, University of Granada, and Humboldt University of Berlin, and held a post at Heidelberg University in 1943.
